queue.title: Powered adaptive breadth replication
queue.hypothesis: The frozen COMBO2 breadth gate retains or improves width-2 causal recovery while using materially less inference compute on unseen worlds.
queue.frozen_rule: spawn second swarm iff baseline unique proposals <=4 OR normalized top-score margin <0.15
queue.design: Run 24 additional unseen worlds with RNG-isolated ONE, TWO, and frozen COMBO2. Aggregate with the original 24 prospective worlds to n=48. Primary analysis is recovery/compute Pareto comparison; no threshold changes permitted.

established_findings: Unconditional two-step search does not improve the primary metric after RNG isolation and costs roughly 9x compute.
Initial-state and local-margin depth gates failed to justify deeper search.
Uniform width-2 proposal breadth improves edge recovery over width-1 across combined n=72 matched worlds, with bootstrap CI excluding zero, at roughly 2x compute.
The width-2 gain is a portfolio effect rather than one globally best extra role.

A frozen adaptive breadth gate is a promising Pareto candidate at prospective n=24, with better mean recovery than ONE/TWO and about 19% less compute than TWO, but recovery effects remain statistically unresolved.
dynamic_enqueue_rules: Every completed experiment must generate at least one next candidate unless a stronger queued candidate already tests the same uncertainty.
Falsification never empties the queue; it narrows or redirects it.
Do not enqueue equivalent retries without a changed causal hypothesis, state representation, reward, search depth, world model, or evaluation design.
Promote surprising anomalies and control victories into diagnostic experiments.
Maintain matched resource budgets and preserve all negative results.
